codeReview.summary: The commit improves duplicate-connection guarding, but the manual-disconnect path still leaves an in-flight async connect uncancelled and cleanup can leave `connected` stuck at `true`. Those gaps mean the hook still misses the requested reconnect/disconnect reliability behavior.

issues.description: `disconnect()` passes `cleanupConnection({ current: false }, ...)`, which only marks a brand-new object as cancelled. The real effect-scoped `cancelled` flag created at line 329 is unchanged, so if `connectWebSocket()` is still awaiting `getToken()` it continues past line 223, creates a socket, and can flip `connected` back to true after an explicit disconnect. The intentional-disconnect race this feature was supposed to close is therefore still reproducible.

`cleanupConnection()` closes the socket and clears refs, but it never calls `setConnected(false)`. When effect cleanup runs because `enabled` becomes false or `pauseWhenHidden` hides the page, the `onclose` handler returns early on `cancelled.current` at line 340, so the hook can keep reporting `connected === true` even though the socket was already closed. That violates the requirement that connection state toggles correctly.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `refactor-worker`'s test-first guidance does not match frontend reliability work in this repo, where mission guidance explicitly says there is no frontend test infrastructure.

summary: Reviewed the feature record, handoff, transcript skeleton, skill guidance, commit `15bc613`, and the resulting `frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts`. The duplicate-connection guard got stronger, but two blocking correctness issues remain in manual disconnect cancellation and `connected` state cleanup, so the review fails.
